issues.legal_issue: The permissible area is subject to both a standard-acre limit and an ordinary-acre ceiling, even when the holding is below the standard-acre limit.
material_facts: Each allottee held about 24 standard acres, but the holdings exceeded 60 ordinary acres when converted.
The allottees relied on their holdings being below 30 standard acres to claim small-landowner status and seek a tenant’s ejectment.
issues.conclusion: The ordinary-acre ceiling applies even where the holding is below 30 standard acres; the definition does not guarantee an irreducible minimum of 30 standard acres.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(3) of the Punjab Security of Lands Tenure Act, 1953, sets a limit of 30 standard acres or, where conversion produces a greater area, 60 ordinary acres. A standard acre reflects the qualitative features of the land, while the ordinary-acre maximum reflects the quantitative limit.

predicates.is_land_tenure_permissible_area_determin: The proceeding requires the permissible area of a landowner or tenant to be determined under a land-tenure regime.
predicates.converted_holding_exceeds_ordinary_area_: The holding, when converted from standard acres into ordinary acres, exceeds the applicable ordinary-acre ceiling.
predicates.permissible_area_is_limited_by_ordinary_: The permissible area is limited by the ordinary-acre ceiling despite the holding being below the standard-acre limit.

issues.definition: When a land-tenure permissible-area determination involves a holding whose converted area exceeds the ordinary-acre ceiling, the permissible area is limited by that ceiling.

issues.legal_issue: Heirs of a displaced person cannot claim the special permissible-area treatment for displaced persons merely because land was allotted to their deceased predecessor.
material_facts: The father was a displaced person who died after migrating to India, and land was allotted in his name after his death.
The land was later transferred and permanent rights were conferred in the names of his sons.
The sons had not owned or abandoned land in the territory from which their father was displaced, and each held more than 60 ordinary acres.
issues.conclusion: The sons were heirs, not displaced persons eligible for the special treatment under proviso (ii) to section 2(3). The explanation excluded heirs and successors from that treatment, so they were assessed under the general definition and were not small landowners because their holdings exceeded the ordinary-acre ceiling.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(3), proviso (ii), of the Punjab Security of Lands Tenure Act, 1953, provides special permissible-area rules for displaced persons; its Explanation excludes their heirs and successors. Section 2(11) adopts the meaning of “displaced person” in the East Punjab Displaced Persons (Land Resettlement) Act, 1949, which requires the person to have held and abandoned land in the relevant territory.

predicates.is_land_tenure_permissible_area_determin: The proceeding requires the permissible area of a landowner or tenant to be determined under a land-tenure regime.
predicates.land_was_allotted_to_displaced_person_he: Land originally associated with a displaced person was allotted to that person’s heir or successor.
predicates.heir_did_not_personally_qualify_as_displ: The heir or successor did not personally hold and abandon land in the territory from which the predecessor was displaced.
predicates.displaced_person_area_concession_is_unav: The heir or successor cannot use the special permissible-area treatment available to a displaced person.

issues.definition: When land-tenure permissible area is determined for an heir who received land associated with a displaced person but did not personally qualify as one, the special displaced-person treatment is unavailable to the heir.

issues.legal_issue: Uncultivated Banjar and Gair Mumkin areas that are not occupied or let for agricultural or agriculture-subservient purposes are excluded when computing permissible or surplus area.
material_facts: Uncultivated Banjar Qadim, Banjar Jadid and Gair Mumkin areas had been included in calculating the allottees’ holdings.
The extent of those areas was disputed, so the Court directed that it be ascertained and the permissible area recomputed after their exclusion.
issues.conclusion: Banjar Qadim and Banjar Jadid areas that do not meet the statutory definition of land cannot be counted. The extent of the Banjar and Gair Mumkin areas was to be determined and the permissible area recomputed after excluding them.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(8) of the Punjab Security of Lands Tenure Act, 1953, and 2(c) of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887, define land by reference to occupation or letting for agricultural purposes, purposes subservient to agriculture, or pasture. The Court approved Nemi Chand Jain v. Financial Commissioner, Punjab, AIR 1964 Punj. 373, which held that Banjar Qadim and Banjar Jadid not occupied or let for those purposes fall outside the definition of land.

predicates.is_land_tenure_area_computation: The proceeding requires land area to be computed for a land-tenure determination.
predicates.parcels_are_uncultivated_banjar_or_gair_: The parcels being assessed are uncultivated Banjar or Gair Mumkin areas.
predicates.parcels_are_not_occupied_or_let_for_agri: The parcels are not occupied or let for agriculture, purposes subservient to agriculture, or pasture.
predicates.such_parcels_are_excluded_from_area_comp: The parcels are left out when the relevant permissible or surplus area is computed.

issues.definition: In a land-tenure area computation, uncultivated Banjar or Gair Mumkin parcels that are not occupied or let for agricultural purposes are excluded from the computation.
